{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Daniel Willis Bump''' (born 13 May 1952) is a mathematician who is a professor at [[Stanford University]] working in [[representation theory]]. He is a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] since 2015, for "contributions to [[number theory]], representation theory, [[combinatorics]], and [[random matrix theory]], as well as mathematical exposition".<ref name="ams">{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|publisher=ams.org|access-date=2016-05-11}}</ref>

He has a [[Bachelor of Arts]] from [[Reed College]], where he graduated in 1974.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/daniel-bump |title=Daniel Bump's Profile |publisher=Stanford Profiles |access-date=25 April 2019}}</ref> He obtained his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1982 under the supervision of [[Walter Lewis Baily, Jr.]]<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=36902|title=Daniel Willis Bump}}</ref> Among Bump's doctoral students is president of the [[National Association of Mathematicians]], [[Edray Goins]].

[https://www.wstein.org/sage_summer/bsd_comp/Bump-Friedberg-Hoffstein-Nonvanishing_theorems_of_L-functions_of_modular_forms_and_their_derivates.pdf "Nonvanishing theorems for L-functions of modular forms and their derivatives"]. ''[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]'', 102(1), pp.&nbsp;543–618.
* Bump, D., & [[David Ginzburg|Ginzburg, D. ]](1992). "Symmetric square L-functions on GL(''r'')". ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'', 136(1), pp.&nbsp;137–205. {{doi|10.2307/2946548}}
* Bump, D., Friedberg, S., & Hoffstein, J. (1996). "On some applications of automorphic forms to number theory", ''Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society'', 33(2), pp.&nbsp;157–175. {{doi|10.1090/S0273-0979-96-00654-4}}
* Bump, D., Choi, K. K., Kurlberg, P., & Vaaler, J. (2000). [http://www.cecm.sfu.ca/~choi/paper/lrh.pdf "A local Riemann hypothesis, I"]. ''Mathematische Zeitschrift'', 233(1), pp. 1–18.
* Bump, D., & [[Persi Diaconis|Diaconis, P.]] (2002). [https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.90.6626&rep=rep1&type=pdf "Toeplitz minors"]. ''Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A'', 97(2), pp. 252–271.
* Bump, D., [[Alexander Gamburd|Gamburd, A.]] (2006). ''On the averages of characteristic polynomials from classical groups'', ''Commun. Math. Phys.'', 265(1), pp. 227–274. {{doi|10.1007/s00220-006-1503-1}}
* Brubaker, B., Bump, D., & Friedberg, S. (2011). ''Schur polynomials and the Yang-Baxter equation'', ''Commun. Math. Phys.'', 308(2), pp. 281–301. {{doi|10.1007/s00220-011-1345-3}}
